requirement: In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.roles`.
rationale:
The source and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.references.book_badges`.

Obligation mapping:

- **Render valid inline references for each of `impl`, `cite`, and `test` as Shields.io static images; display the role and full name; provide meaningful alt text.** `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_references]` reaches `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_inline_references]` and `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_badge]`. These use `src/lib.rs#impl[ReferenceKind]` and `src/lib.rs#fn[shield_badge]` to generate role-labelled Shields.io images with `alt="<role> <full name>"`. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition]` checks all three roles and their image URLs. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names]` tests the shared image generator's URL and full-name alt text.
- **Render valid fenced references as badges, followed by their bodies as Markdown.** `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_references]` inserts the badge before the body and preserves Markdown processing by separating the HTML wrapper and body with blank lines. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fenced_references_render_their_badge_and_body_and_built_ins_are_unlinked]` checks the linked badge, alt text, ordering, and retained Markdown body, including a reference nested within a definition. Fenced references use the same role-specific badge generator as inline references.
- **Link references to the corresponding requirement or example definition badge; make links work across chapters, including nested chapters.** `src/lib.rs#fn[reference_badge]` uses the target definition's path and kind-specific anchor, through `src/lib.rs#impl[DefinitionKind]` and `src/lib.rs#fn[chapter_href]`. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition]` verifies nested-to-root requirement links and the destination anchor. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them]` verifies the corresponding example link and anchor. The fenced-reference test also checks a same-chapter link.
- **Render fenced requirement and example directives as Shields.io definition images identifying their respective kinds.** `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` calls the shared image generator with the kind label from `src/lib.rs#impl[DefinitionKind]`. The definition tests `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` and `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them`, under `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]`, exercise both directive kinds; the latter asserts the example image's identifying alt text. The shared Shields.io generator is directly tested by `shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names`.
- **Keep text outside directives literal.** `src/lib.rs#fn[replace_definitions]` copies intervening and trailing slices unchanged. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal]` explicitly checks retained surrounding text and the literal legacy inline form. The example and fenced-reference tests additionally check protected code examples and invalid or unknown forms remaining literal.
- **Keep badge text legible for both visited and unvisited links.** `md/habeas.css` uses image badges and identical inherited-color, undecorated styling for both link states. `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[badge_stylesheet_keeps_visited_links_legible_and_shows_focus]` checks equality of those declarations.
- **Show a visible keyboard-focus indicator.** `md/habeas.css` supplies a two-pixel outline with an offset for `:focus-visible`; the same stylesheet test asserts a nonzero, non-disabled outline.

The permitted inline layout, hover brightening, fenced-reference block styling, and built-in help cursor are implemented in `md/habeas.css`. Built-in unlinked badges are specified by `requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, which `replace_references` also marks as implemented. Definition detail links and “See evidence” output are specified by `requirements.index.navigation`, also marked on `replace_definitions`. No unacknowledged gap was found.

text: :::{req} book_badges

In a book chapter, each valid `{impl}`, `{cite}`, or `{test}` reference, inline or fenced, MUST render as a Shields.io static badge image with meaningful alt text that displays its role and full name and links to the badge at the corresponding `{req}` or `{example}` definition. Links MUST work across chapters, including nested chapters. A fenced reference MUST render its badge followed by its body as Markdown. Each fenced `{req}` or `{example}` directive MUST render as a Shields.io definition badge image identifying its kind; text outside a directive MUST remain literal. Badge text MUST remain legible regardless of whether its link has been visited. A badge link MUST show a visible indicator when it has keyboard focus and MAY brighten on hover. Badges MAY be laid out inline with the surrounding text, a fenced reference's badge and body MAY be visually set apart from the surrounding text as one block, and a built-in's unlinked badge MAY show a help cursor to signal its hover text. These badges use the syntax defined by {cite}`requirements.references.roles`.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} navigation

Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
:::{req} definition

An mdBook chapter MAY define an example with an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{example} <name>` and a closing colon-only fence of at least the opening length. The full name MUST use the same chapter-derived namespace and valid-name rules as `{req}`. The body MUST include all Markdown between the fences, excluding surrounding whitespace, and MUST describe a concrete case with expected behavior. An example MUST contain at least one valid `{cite}` or `{test}` reference to a requirement it illustrates; `{cite}` makes the requirement an input to the example's assessment, and `{test}` makes the example an input to the requirement's assessment, under {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. An example MAY use both. An example directive inside a fenced code block MUST remain literal.
:::{req} index

When a `{requirements-index}` chapter exists, it MUST list examples as well as requirements, identify each entry's kind, and show each example's evidence state. Example detail pages and their links MUST follow {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages` and {cite}`requirements.index.navigation`; references to an example MUST link to its definition.
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
